facts: This appeal u/s. 2(j)(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970 is directed against a judgment dated the 11th July, 1975 of a Division Bench of the High Court of Bombay setting aside the acquittal recorded by the Additional Sessions Judge, Latur of 8 appellant and convicting them of offences u/ss. 147 and 148 and S. 302 read with S. 149 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860...
The occurrence took place on the 30th December, 1971 and Amirali, a step-brother of Shahabuddin (P.W. 1) lost his life in consequence.
17 person were tried by the learned Additional Sessions Judge for the offences mentioned above as also one under S. 302 read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860...

The trial ended in acquittal of all the accused with the judgment dated October 11, 1972 rendered by the learned Additional Sessions Judge which was, however, set aside in the case of the 8 appellants by the High Court as stated above.
All the 17 accused are residents of village Janval in Osmanabad District of the State of Maharashtra
At about 8-00 a.m. on the 30th December, 1971 the wife of one Suleman, a resident of village Janval, quarreled with his sister and he brought home the deceased to pacify the two ladies.
Accused Nos. 1, 3, 15 and 16 went in the company of each other to the house of the deceased and challenged him to come out.
The autopsy was carried out Dr. Madhukar Kulkarni (P.W. 11) on the next day.
Sixteen witnesses were produced at the trial in support of the prosecution case.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in setting aside the acquittal recorded by the Additional Sessions Judge and convicting the appellants?
What is the test to be applied for accepting the testimony of eye-witnesses?
petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the parties
Implicit reliance cannot be placed on the testimony of Shahabuddin (P.W. 1) Ismail (P.W. 5)

We need not give the details of those improvements as they have been adverted to by the learned trial Judge and it is conceded by learned counsel for the State that the depositions of these two witnesses do suffer from that defect.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution case may briefly be stated thus.
The learned Judges of the Division Bench, however, saw no reason to doubt the testimony of Shahabuddin (P.W. 1) and Ismail (P.W. 5)
They proceeded to analyse the evidence of Muktabai (P.W. 4) and Nama (P.W. 9) and did not attach much importance to the omission therefrom of the names of some of the accused.
court_reasoning: The application of these principles to the available evidence, in their opinion, established the participation of the 8 appellants in the occurrence and that is why they convicted and sentenced them as stated earlier

We propose to look for assuring circumstances for their testimony in the case of each of the appellants and to confirm the conviction of only those of latter whose guilt as testified to by Shahabuddin (P.W. 1) and Ismail (P.W. 5) finds support from reliable evidence
holding: The conviction and sentence imposed on the appellants are hereby confirmed.
